title: Pro Drafter Helps Me Dominate in Reality Fracture Draft!!! (ft. @limitedlevel-ups)
player_note: NicolaiBolas drafts (his name is on the banner); the guest Alex Nikolic (Limited Level-Ups) advises. Captions are unlabelled; the idea `speaker` field credits the guest, the host or both from content.
event: FRA live Arena draft, best of three ('this is best of three, so if we see the sideboard cards, we can actually take them'); Premier / Traditional not named on screen
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/8BzUchj9HuA (banner and pack title strips; the pool at P2p1 (13 + 1 sideboard) and the 45/40 and 40/40 deck screens at 1640 and 2012 s); pack lists read from images that loaded; takes confirmed by the pool, the deck screens and the transcript, except P3p6, P3p10 and P3p12 (not shown; taken null); transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; nothing past 33:35 read; cut-off 2020 s

colour_path.quote: we're going to diverge from our first pick probably
the sultai space is so much better for the graveyard stuff.
it's looking like green white might be a good spot.
the packs are pushing us enough in the direction of white that we should probably listen.
we are getting into a bit of a go wide theme
Huge fan of Twisted Fates ... We have the black fixing to be able to cast it.

colour_path.main: GW with a light black splash (Twisted Fates x2, one Swamp)
colour_path.quote: I would like to definitely would like to not play a second swamp.

picks.reasoning: Carnivorous Cultivator, the rare: a two-mana 2/3 deathtouch that can draw a land. The guest also likes Clash of Elements (gold removal) but monocoloured over gold is an upside if close; he would take Memory Trap if the rare were absent.

considered.Clash of Elements: guest: the other card he likes; strong gold removal, but monocolour over gold when close
considered.Memory Trap: white removal, the option if the rare were missing

quotes: as always, I think monocolored over gold is definitely an upside. So, if it's close, I like taking the monocolor card, but I'm not afraid of taking the strong gold cards.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment: guest calls it phenomenal (pretty good on four, really good late, can be self-milled to draw it free) and a card that plays with the Cultivator because any self-mill helps both. Nicolai notes no green card in the pack.

considered.Carnivorous Cultivator: guest: plays with Recruitment because any self-mill helps both

quotes: I think this card is phenomenal. It's just, you know, pretty good on four, really good late.

picks.reasoning: Primal Witchstalker: the guest has been super impressed (three-mana 2/1 menace that ramps, sometimes a three-for-one). Clash of Elements is in the pack again.

considered.Prophesied End: guest likes it more than the usual destroy-tapped removal

quotes: the fact that it ramps you means you're totally fine with the body. And sometimes it's like a three for one almost.

picks.reasoning: Simulacrum Shaper: fits the self-mill pool and is 'a little bit surprising' to see fourth. The guest also calls out Violent Echoes (exceptional) and Theorix Charm; the pack is a mixed signal (three good red cards, Pia, a Vinelasher).

considered.Violent Echoes: guest: exceptional, kill a creature draw a card

quotes: Um I think we're probably taking it here for our deck. It seems like it fits.

picks.reasoning: Vinelasher Adept, the green landcycler: the guest has been really high on landcyclers (good at fixing and good to cast). Red seems open with three good red cards in a row but they pull only into non-green red.
quotes: I like the green land cyclinger. I've been really high on land cyclingers.

picks.reasoning: Generous Revival over No Admittance: it plays nicely in the graveyard plan; the guest likes adding colours to layer synergies rather than for raw power ('adding white because we have a really nice tool for a graveyard deck'). Nicolai floated taking No Admittance.

considered.No Admittance: pick six, red open; Nicolai's alternative

picks.plan: Green-black graveyard with a white layer.
quotes: one thing I like to do with drafting this set as I'm drafting a multicolor deck is I don't mind adding colors, not necessarily even for omega powerful cards, but to layer on your synergies.

picks.reasoning: Bestial Incursion over Vigorbloom Charm and a land: a nice synergy card, good on rate, and the guest has been taking good spells over fixing in pack one because there is plenty of fixing in the set.

considered.Transformative Commons: land, passed here and taken next pick

quotes: I've been taking good spells over fixing in pack one anyways.

picks.reasoning: Transformative Commons over Paradox Shaper and Bloombrute: the Shaper is tempting with the self-mill but there are better cards that help you mill; the guest also says the red cards do not play well with their green. Bloombrute would be green-white.

considered.Paradox Shaper: pretty tempting but better cards help you mill

quotes: I think here is where I would take a land.

picks.reasoning: Konstrari Annex (land): agreed to take a land; the red cards 'don't really play all that well with our green cards'.
quotes: Yeah, I agree. Yeah, let's take a land.

picks.reasoning: Surgical Precision: they have no removal and the guest is happy to splash fishing removal like this. Warrior's Blades and Massacre Girl in the pack.
quotes: I like surgical precision. We don't have any removal right now and I've been happy to splash removal like this one.

picks.reasoning: Way of the Healer, late: the guest finds it really good; a green-white lane may be forming, and Nicolai could 'totally see us pivoting to green white'.
quotes: way of healer is really good. I think I would take it here.
Yeah, I could totally see us pivoting to green white.

picks.reasoning: Fateshaper Aspirant over Tether Technician; they note they could have two lands for a good red card. Not discussed further.
Innovative Commons (second land for a possible splash); Heartstring Puller was the other card.
Last card, Swamp, auto-selected.

Guiding Hydra over Your Fate Ends Here: the guest says they are really close, the Hydra is the higher-upside card and he could regret it if they do not see removal; Nicolai expects to get Surgical Precision back from the pack (three white cards there).

considered.Surgical Precision: expected to wheel as a removal consolation

quotes: I would go for the higher upside card right now, but I could see us maybe regretting this if we maybe don't see as much removal as we'd like.

picks.reasoning: Memory Trap over Rewrite Regrets: the graveyard theming has been minimal for a while and the packs keep pushing towards white; Memory Trap is the best white card they could take, and Rewrite Regrets is phenomenal with the landcyclers but they are moving away from it.

considered.Rewrite Regrets: guest: phenomenal with the landcyclers, but the graveyard theme is fading
considered.Prudent Fateseer: in the pack (taken next time round)

quotes: I think the packs are pushing us enough in the direction of white that we should probably listen.

picks.reasoning: Prudent Fateseer over a blue-black land and Tetsuko: no green-white cards he loves; the guest finds the 1/4 decent and they are getting into a go-wide theme with the Hydra and Way of the Healer.
quotes: I think I would take the fate seer here, the one four because I think that card is pretty decent and we are getting into a bit of a go wide theme.

picks.reasoning: Sureshot Sower, the two-drop green 3/1: a fine role-player, they are a little low on two-mana cards; Unsummon also considered (good against beast and dragon tokens).

considered.Unsummon: guest: really good against the big tokens

quotes: I like the two drop the green three one there. It's a fine role player. We are a little bit low on two mana cards at this point.

picks.reasoning: Teyo, Lightshield Expert: great cheap flash spell, rarely cast on two but can trade a two-drop when on the back foot; over Fatehold Chronologist and Inspired Tethermage (which has impressed the guest).

considered.Fatehold Chronologist: two-drop that works with the go-wide plan

quotes: I like taking Teyo here. Teyo is just great. It's another cheap spell.

picks.reasoning: Something Worth Saving over Yoshimaru and a land: the guest wants it for the graveyard stuff they do have and to find their good cards (there is a decent gap between the great cards and the medium cards).
quotes: just being able to find your good cards while binning flashback cards has been something I liked.

picks.reasoning: Blossom-Blessed Angel over Germinate Recruits: the Recruits is really hard to do; they pass Bloombrute earlier, and note there is no life gain in the deck.

considered.Germinate Recruits: really hard to do, needs lifelinkers

quotes: I think we take the blossom blessed angel.

picks.reasoning: Afterthought Sentry (colourless two-drop) 'has been playable'; it lets them take better expensive cards in pack three and is a sideboard card for best of three against recursive recruitments.
quotes: this lets us take better expensive cards in pack three. And also this is best of three, so it could be a good sideboard card.

picks.reasoning: Arcane Amphisbaena over Budding Insurgent: better in a slower deck, good even in an average midrange deck.
quotes: I like the Amphisbaena. It's better in a slower graveyard deck but even in your average midrange deck it's good.

picks.reasoning: Apex Witchstalker over Way of the Mentor: they say it will not make the cut but something weird could happen in pack three (a great black card).

considered.Way of the Mentor: not very good with no lifegain

quotes: I don't think it's going to make the cut here, but something weird could happen in pack three.

picks.reasoning: Ferocity of the Hunt from the wheel pack; pack-one Tetsuko pair also there.
quotes: Here I'll take ferocity of the hunt.

picks.reasoning: Teyo, Diamondblade Mage wheeled; 'Nice late'.
quotes: Nice late.

picks.reasoning: Meticulous Commons over Theorix Metamage; no comment.
Last card, Cast Away Doubt, auto-selected.

Liliana the Faultless (white one-mana 1/1 that gains life and protects another creature) over Liliana the Repentant: the guest likes both, takes the white one and is happy to stay on the white path; they may still open good black cards. Surgical Precision, Primal Witchstalker and a land are also in the pack; Nicolai guesses white drafters at the table took the white cards from the first pack.
quotes: I like both these Lilas. I think I would take the white one here.

picks.reasoning: Koth of the Homestead over Wrecking Gecko and Flourishing Grapple: 'let's take Koth and get the burn white'; Nicolai likes the rare too. Now they have more life-gain cards.
quotes: Koth has been okay. I also like the rare, but let's take Koth.

picks.reasoning: Twisted Fates over Restore with Empathy and Pia, Determined Rebuilder: the guest is a huge fan of it, they are low on removal and have a graveyard theme and black fixing (land) to cast it.
quotes: Huge fan of Twisted Fates and huge fan of it here where we're a little bit low on removal.

picks.reasoning: Unflinching Hortimancer (two-mana 2/1) over Something Worth Saving: in a deck not super graveyard focused they only want one SWS; Hortimancer gives more life gain and can win games with Liliana.

considered.Something Worth Saving: only one wanted; two is the sweet spot at best

quotes: In a deck like this where we're not super graveyard focused, I only want to play one. I think we take Hortimancer though.

picks.reasoning: Way of the Healer over the green-white gold card Bloombrute: the deck is not doing the life-gain thing, and Healer helps them go wide.

considered.Bloombrute: green-white gold card, not for this deck

quotes: I think way of the healer is great. This is a perfect example of what is your deck doing.

picks.reasoning: Taken card unknown: the pack held Wrecking Gecko, Flourishing Grapple, Tenured Tethermage, Koth, Paradox Shaper and Vigorbloom Annex. The guest says it is close between the land and the sideboard card ('I take these sideboard cards pretty highly when I'm drafting best of three'), and picks the sideboard card (a huge upgrade over a game-one card); the card taken is not shown.
quotes: I take these sideboard cards pretty highly when I'm drafting best of three. So I would be on the sideboard card.

picks.reasoning: Prudent Fateseer again: 'that's great, nice with the plan'; Mabel is not as good as Mabel, Valley Hero.
quotes: Yep. I think that's great.

picks.reasoning: Twisted Fates, second copy: with the Swamp, a dual land, the Aspirant and the Cultivator they have about five black sources for two cards.
quotes: we have four sources of fixing if you count the swamp we're going to play to find with the adept.

picks.reasoning: Pia, Aether Ascetic over Primal Witchstalker (which wheeled) and Heartstring Puller: they have two Ways of the Healer, enough enchantments for Pia to return one and for Memory Trap.

considered.Wrecking Gecko: seen at the next pick, passed for going smaller

quotes: when you have exactly this split, I would take Pia.

picks.reasoning: Taken card unknown (pack: Flourishing Grapple, Predictive Preparations, Tethermage's Advantage, Wrecking Gecko, Mountain). He says the sideboard card came back and Gecko has been better than he thought but they are going a little smaller than that.

considered.Wrecking Gecko: guest: better than expected, but too big for them

quotes: I think Gecko has been better than I thought it would be, but I feel like we're just going a little smaller than that.

picks.reasoning: Restore with Empathy from the pack of Awaken the Inferno and Skilled Battlecarver; they would play it only in the graveyard deck, so it is a sideboard-level pick.
quotes: If we were in the graveyard deck, I would play it, but not for this deck so much.

picks.reasoning: Taken card unknown: the three cards left from the pick-4 pack were never readable; the pick is not shown.
Overgrown Farmland, the rare land with two cards in the pack: 'rare land with two cards in the pack is huge pickup for us'.
quotes: That's a nice pickup. Rare land with two cards in the pack.

picks.reasoning: Last card, Titanbones, Towering Heart, auto-selected; Nicolai tells how an opponent once discarded it to survive.
